title: Design a Configuration Validator for Nested Key-Value Systems
statement: You are building a configuration validator for a system that uses dot-separated keys to represent nested settings (e.g., `database.host.port`, `logging.level.console`). The validator must support two operations: setting a value at a key path, and checking whether a given key path is explicitly set (not inherited from parents). A key is considered explicitly set only if a value was directly assigned to it via the `set` operation, not if it only exists due to a parent being set. Implement a class `ConfigValidator` with: `void set(String key, String value)` to assign a value at the given key path, and `boolean isExplicitlySet(String key)` to return true if and only if the key has been directly set via a prior `set` call. Key paths consist of lowercase alphanumeric characters and dots, with no consecutive dots or leading/trailing dots. Values are non-empty strings.
summary: Track explicitly set keys in a dot-separated hierarchical configuration system.
constraints: Key paths use only [a-z0-9.] with valid dot separation

examples.input: ConfigValidator cv = new ConfigValidator(); cv.set('a.b.c', 'value1'); cv.set('a.b', 'value2'); boolean b1 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a'); boolean b2 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b'); boolean b3 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b.c'); boolean b4 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b.c.d');
examples.explanation: 'a' was never directly set. 'a.b' and 'a.b.c' were set explicitly. 'a.b.c.d' was never set.

examples.input: ConfigValidator cv = new ConfigValidator(); cv.set('x.y.z', 'val'); boolean r1 = cv.isExplicitlySet('x'); boolean r2 = cv.isExplicitlySet('x.y'); boolean r3 = cv.isExplicitlySet('x.y.z'); boolean r4 = cv.isExplicitlySet('x.y.z.w');
examples.explanation: Only the exact key 'x.y.z' was set explicitly.

testcases.input: ConfigValidator cv = new ConfigValidator(); cv.set('a.b.c', 'value1'); cv.set('a.b', 'value2'); boolean b1 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a'); boolean b2 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b'); boolean b3 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b.c'); boolean b4 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b.c.d');

ConfigValidator cv = new ConfigValidator(); cv.set('x.y.z', 'val'); boolean r1 = cv.isExplicitlySet('x'); boolean r2 = cv.isExplicitlySet('x.y'); boolean r3 = cv.isExplicitlySet('x.y.z'); boolean r4 = cv.isExplicitlySet('x.y.z.w');
ConfigValidator cv = new ConfigValidator(); boolean r = cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b');

ConfigValidator cv = new ConfigValidator(); cv.set('a', 'val'); boolean r1 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a'); cv.set('a.b', 'val2'); boolean r2 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a'); boolean r3 = cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b');

ConfigValidator cv = new ConfigValidator(); cv.set('a.b.c.d', 'deep'); cv.set('a.b', 'shallow'); int count = 0; if (cv.isExplicitlySet('a')) count++; if (cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b')) count++; if (cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b.c')) count++; if (cv.isExplicitlySet('a.b.c.d')) count++;

io_template.Python: class ConfigValidator: def set(self, key: str, value: str) -> None: pass def isExplicitlySet(self, key: str) -> bool: pass
